stacks.title: The three-city spring trip
stacks.summary: Two people with a fortnight in April and three cities on the list, one conversation: ask TravelCharika how each city scores in April, from ten years of measured climate, holidays, crowds and fares, and whether May would suit them better (it scores 87 places, so check the three are among them); give Stopover the home airport, the cities and the window so it prices every order of the cities and every departure day and returns the cheapest route, with the flight or train for each leg and a link to book it; look on Booking.com for somewhere to stay on the nights that route gives; put the legs on Google Calendar. One new connector that works out the order and the day to leave, three already on the list that say when to go and hold the beds and the dates; nothing here buys a ticket. Stopover reached the list through a contributor's pull request (#53).
stacks.status: Status: composed, not yet field-tested against a real trip. If you run it, send a Field Report (see CONTRIBUTING).

stacks.title: The back-room gig night
stacks.summary: A UK pub putting on a monthly Friday gig in its back room, one Desktop conversation: check TBC Events for what else is on in town that Friday so the night doesn't clash, search GigXchange for performers free that date, read their press kits and check the GX Index for what a pub gig typically pays, then make a booking offer from the pub's member account where offers are enabled; put the night and the load-in time on Google Calendar and draft the regulars' newsletter in Gmail. Two new connectors that know the local listings and the grassroots circuit, two proven ones that hold the date and the mailing list, with Claude carrying the details between them. The fee conversation and the sound check stay with the people.
stacks.status: Status: composed, not yet field-tested against a live booking. If you run it, send a Field Report (see CONTRIBUTING).

stacks.title: The kitchen-table bills night
stacks.summary: A US household working through its recurring bills, one Desktop conversation: find the latest internet, mobile and insurance bills in Gmail, get Lower My Bill's provider-specific call script for each and its reminder to call before a promotional rate ends, check in Zeno Household whether the savings change next month's cash-flow forecast and leave a budget note for a partner, then put the call reminders on Google Calendar. Two new connectors that know the negotiation playbook and the household's numbers, two proven ones that hold the bills and the dates, with Claude carrying the list between them. The calls themselves stay with the person.
stacks.status: Status: composed, not yet field-tested against a live set of bills. If you run it, send a Field Report (see CONTRIBUTING).

stacks.title: The medical-bill and appeal night
stacks.summary: The person in the household who handles the medical paperwork, one Desktop conversation: pull the itemized ER bill and the insurer's Explanation of Benefits from the family folder in Google Drive, run each line of the bill through Med Bill Check against the Medicare rate for the state, decode the denial code on the EOB with Appeal My Claim and check the appeal deadline for that plan type, have Appeal My Claim draft the appeal letter and Med Bill Check draft a financial-assistance request to the hospital, then put the appeal deadline and a follow-up reminder on Google Calendar. Two new connectors that know the billing and appeal rules, two proven ones that hold the paperwork and the dates, with Claude carrying the case between them. Both letters come out as drafts for the person to review and send.
stacks.status: Status: composed, not yet field-tested against a live bill. If you run it, send a Field Report (see CONTRIBUTING).

stacks.title: The small-firm litigator's Monday
stacks.summary: Monday, one Desktop conversation: ask Case Status which matters have overdue tasks and which clients are waiting on a reply, pull the opinion and docket behind the ruling a client is asking about from CourtListener, run the draft opposition's citations through lawdiver to confirm each case is still good law, send the client a plain-language update through Case Status, then log the morning to the right matters in PointOne with each entry checked against that client's billing guidelines before it goes out. Four connectors that each hold one piece of the practice — the client file, the public record, the citator, the timesheet — with Claude carrying the matter across all four.
stacks.status: Status: composed, not yet field-tested against a live practice. If you run it, send a Field Report (see CONTRIBUTING).

stacks.title: The one-person supply chain
stacks.summary: Tuesday, one Desktop conversation: ask Terminal49 which inbound containers are still sitting at the port and pull the event history behind the one that slipped, check Stord for stock at the facility about to run the promotion and which retailer missed on-time-in-full last week, price the pallet to Spain in LetMeShip with duties estimated before committing, then rank PostCo's return reasons by SKU and ask the question none of the four dashboards can answer alone — is the SKU we're about to reorder the one customers keep sending back. Four connectors that each see one leg of the chain, with Claude holding the whole route.
stacks.status: Status: composed, not yet field-tested against a live operation. If you run it, send a Field Report (see CONTRIBUTING).

stacks.title: The solo Shopify operator
stacks.summary: Monday morning, one Cowork conversation: pull last week's real profit from Metorik (sales minus costs, not vanity revenue), read which price test won in Intelligems, ask AfterShip where returns are eating margin, then put Meta Ads spend next to it all and ask the question none of the four dashboards can answer alone — which campaign looks great on ROAS but ships the most returns. Four connectors that each know one corner of the store, with Claude holding the whole picture.
stacks.status: Status: composed, not yet field-tested against a live store. If you run it, send a Field Report (see CONTRIBUTING).
